notes: Xcel facts read on 2026-09-29 from Xcel's own pages and its 2026 Rebate Summary PDF (effective Oct 1, 2026). Do not state those as verified. facts.program: Xcel Energy cold-climate air source heat pump
facts.claim: $750 per heating ton at 5°F standard; $1,500 per ton with the gas-home bonus
facts.eligibility: Xcel electric or gas customers in Colorado; participating contractor. Bonus for homes heated with Xcel natural gas, effective Oct 1, 2026. Electric-heat homes (e.g. baseboards) get the standard amount only.
facts.dates: Effective Oct 1, 2026; install invoiced by Dec 31, 2026, applications through Sep 30, 2027
facts.notes: The old $2,250 per ton / $9,000 figure came from an earlier rate sheet and is wrong for 2026.

facts.program: Xcel Energy air source heat pump (ducted)
facts.claim: $300 per cooling ton standard; $600 with bonus
facts.eligibility: Same as above
facts.dates: Effective Oct 1, 2026

facts.program: Xcel Energy heat pump water heater
facts.claim: $750 standard; $1,500 with bonus
facts.eligibility: ENERGY STAR, 3.3 UEF
facts.dates: Effective Oct 1, 2026
facts.notes: The old $2,250 flat figure is wrong.

facts.program: Xcel Energy smart thermostat
facts.eligibility: ENERGY STAR rated

facts.program: Xcel Energy insulation and air sealing
facts.claim: 30% of cost: up to $500 attic, $350 wall, $400 air sealing; gas customers 1.5 times
facts.eligibility: Xcel gas or electric heat
facts.notes: Taken from the same rebate sheet as our /programs/xcel-energy-colorado-rebates/ page.

facts.program: Xcel Energy EV charger and wiring rebate
facts.claim: Up to $500 for a Level 2 charger and/or 240V wiring; standard rebate up to $800 in a Disproportionately Impacted Community; up to $2,300 income-qualified
facts.eligibility: Enroll in Optimize Your Charge first. EV Accelerate At Home closed to new Colorado applications on July 14, 2026.
facts.dates: 2026, first come first served
facts.notes: The old '$1,300' figure added $500 + $800 and is wrong. Not re-read 2026-10-03 (blocked: page loads by JavaScript); verified 2026-09-29.

facts.program: Xcel Energy Renewable Battery Connect
facts.claim: General: $250 per kW AC of max continuous discharge power, up to $5,000; income-qualified $1,000 per kW; DIC $500 per kW (IQ and DIC capped at 75% of equipment cost); plus $100 a year for 5 years
facts.eligibility: Tesla Powerwall or current Enphase batteries; solar-charged; Xcel controls the battery during peak events
facts.dates: Reopened May 21, 2026; general budget $13.6M with $11.3M left on Sep 1, 2026
facts.notes: Not re-read 2026-10-03 (blocked: page loads by JavaScript); verified 2026-09-29.

facts.program: Xcel Energy Solar*Rewards (residential, 2026)
facts.claim: 2026 residential products are income-qualified and Disproportionately Impacted Community only: $1 per watt up to 10 kW AC upfront. Everyone else gets net metering only, no upfront rebate.
facts.amount: $1 per watt up to 10 kW (IQ/DIC only)
facts.eligibility: Xcel customers
facts.dates: Opened May 21, 2026
facts.notes: The old '$300 per kW, up to $1,500' figure is wrong for general customers.

facts.program: Federal residential clean energy credits (25C, 25D)
facts.claim: Ended for spending after Dec 31, 2025
facts.eligibility: All homeowners
facts.dates: Ended Dec 31, 2025
facts.notes: Applies to every state; do not show a 30% federal credit on 2026 installs.

facts.program: Colorado heat pump tax credit (upfront customer discount)
facts.claim: 2026 installs: air-source heat pump tax credit $1,000, of which the customer must get at least $333 off at install; ground, water or combined source $2,000 ($667 minimum discount); heat pump water heater $250 ($83 minimum discount)
facts.eligibility: Any Colorado installation by a contractor registered with the Colorado Energy Office; ENERGY STAR; AHRI matched; space heat pumps designed to meet at least 80% of annual heating needs; no paperwork for the customer
facts.dates: Installed on or after Jan 1, 2026; amounts drop again in tax year 2029
facts.notes: The 2024-2025 amounts ($1,500 air-source, $499.95 minimum discount) have expired. Contractors may keep up to two-thirds of the credit, so the customer discount can be larger than the minimum. Read in the browser pane 2026-10-05.

facts.program: Colorado Home Energy Rebate Program (HEAR single-family)
facts.claim: HEAR single-family program (Region 1 Front Range and Region 2) is closed. Amounts when open: up to $8,000 cold-climate heat pump, $3,000 other heat pump, $1,750 heat pump water heater, $1,600 insulation and air sealing, $4,000 panel, $2,500 wiring, $840 electric stove, $14,000 total per household; 100% of cost below 80% AMI, 50% of cost at 80%-150% AMI
facts.eligibility: Income at or below 150% of county AMI, through a registered contractor
facts.dates: Closed; applications after Aug 1, 2026 not reviewed for Region 2 (updated Aug 2026); small multifamily HEAR and manufactured-home and large multifamily HER planned for 2026
facts.notes: Counties in Region 1 include Adams, Arapahoe, Boulder, Denver, El Paso and Larimer. Page says the Colorado Home Energy Rebates Dashboard shows funding left. Read in the browser pane 2026-10-05.

facts.program: Power Ahead Colorado heat pump rebate (DRCOG)
facts.claim: $1,500 rebate on an ENERGY STAR certified cold-climate air-source heat pump installed in an existing building by a verified Power Ahead Colorado contractor, preapproved before work begins
facts.eligibility: Project in a municipality or county that participates in DRCOG (Adams, Arapahoe, Boulder, Broomfield, Denver, Clear Creek, Douglas, Gilpin, Jefferson and part of Weld); retrofit only, new construction not eligible; single-family, multifamily or commercial; can be combined with other rebates
facts.dates: Launched July 15, 2026 (CPR News); no end date or remaining budget stated on the program page
facts.notes: Ground-source and other heat pump types are not yet covered; the program page says later phases will expand. We did not confirm that every town in those counties participates; the page asks you to check with the program.

facts.program: Colorado Springs Utilities heat pump rebates
facts.claim: ENERGY STAR heat pump $1,500; cold-climate air-source heat pump under 3 tons $1,500; 3 tons and over $3,000; air-to-water heat pump $3,000; electric customers approved for a heat pump under 3 tons also get a $1,500 electric bill credit starting Jan 1, 2026
facts.eligibility: Colorado Springs Utilities electric and/or gas customer; retrofit; NEEP-listed for cold-climate; permit and final inspection with Pikes Peak Regional Building Department; two rebates per service address every three years; ductless systems pay by outdoor unit
facts.dates: Equipment bought and installed Jan 1 to Dec 31, 2026; application postmarked by Jan 31, 2027; first come, first served
facts.notes: Amounts from the 2026 rebate application (version 1.2026) and the HVAC page. The page banner says the $1,500 bill credit applies to customers approved for heat pump rebates under three tons; we did not find how it combines with the $1,500 rebate, so we do not add the two. Rules read at csu.org/rebates-incentives/residential-rules.

facts.program: Colorado Springs Utilities heat pump water heater rebate
facts.claim: $750 for an ENERGY STAR heat pump water heater; natural gas storage water heater $300; natural gas boiler $1,200; natural gas condensing furnace $900
facts.eligibility: Heat pump water heater: Utilities electric customer; retrofit; final inspection with Pikes Peak Regional Building Department; two rebates per address every three years
facts.dates: Installed Jan 1 to Dec 31, 2026; application postmarked by Jan 31, 2027
facts.notes: Rules at csu.org/rebates-incentives/residential-rules. Paid as a credit on the utility account, up to eight weeks.

facts.program: Colorado Springs Utilities insulation rebates
facts.claim: Attic (R-49 with bypass air sealing), wall (R-13 cavity) and crawl space (R-15 continuous) insulation: 40% of total cost, up to $1,250 each
facts.eligibility: Utilities electric and/or gas customer; licensed Colorado contractor (do-it-yourself does not qualify); living space only; total insulation must meet Department of Energy recommendations; homes of four or fewer units, three stories or under
facts.dates: Installed Jan 1 to Dec 31, 2026; application postmarked by Jan 31, 2027
facts.notes: The 40% and $1,250 figures are from the attic and wall rules text; the application form lists the same $1,250 for crawl space.

facts.program: Colorado Springs Utilities smart thermostat and Peak Energy Rewards
facts.claim: Smart thermostat rebate up to $50 (not more than the thermostat cost before tax); Peak Energy Rewards pays $50 the first year and $25 each year after a full cooling season
facts.eligibility: ENERGY STAR thermostat; Utilities electric and/or gas customer; Peak Energy Rewards needs an electric account and a thermostat that controls a central air conditioner
facts.dates: Cooling season May to September; events 1 to 9 p.m. weekdays, up to four hours, no more than 15 a season
facts.notes: Two thermostat rebates per address every three years.

facts.program: Efficiency Works heat pump rebates (Fort Collins Utilities)
facts.claim: Ducted air-source heat pump Tier 1 $1,500 per unit and Tier 2 (cold climate, 8.1 HSPF2) $2,000 per unit; non-ducted $500 per ton, or $1,000 per ton replacing electric baseboard; ground-source $3,000 per unit
facts.eligibility: Residential electric customers of Fort Collins Utilities (also Estes Park, Longmont, Loveland); installed by an Efficiency Works listed provider; home at least one year old; apply within 45 days; incentives over $2,500 need pre-approval or are capped at $2,500
facts.dates: Air-source tiers effective Oct 1, 2026; other measures effective Jan 1, 2026; funding limited
facts.notes: Revised table read 2026-10-05. Total in the sheet's 2-ton example is for illustration only. Rebates plus bonus cannot exceed project cost.

facts.program: Efficiency Works heat pump water heater rebate (Fort Collins Utilities)
facts.claim: $600 replacing an electric or propane water heater; $400 replacing natural gas; ENERGY STAR certified
facts.eligibility: Fort Collins Utilities residential electric customer; retail purchase application within 45 days
facts.dates: Effective Jan 1, 2026
facts.notes: The retrofit sheet lists $600 and $400 as 'per unit'; the retail sheet says 'up to'.

facts.program: Efficiency Works bundling and rental bonuses (Fort Collins Utilities)
facts.claim: $2,000 bundling bonus for a heat pump plus an envelope measure (air sealing, windows, doors) within six months, not counting heat pump water heaters; rental properties served by Fort Collins Utilities get double the standard retrofit rebate with a 12-month lease and preapproval
facts.eligibility: Retrofit Rebate program only; rental bonus does not double the bundling bonus; rebates plus bonus cannot exceed project cost
facts.dates: 2026; funding limited and subject to change

facts.program: Efficiency Works insulation and air sealing (Fort Collins Utilities)
facts.claim: Walls, basement walls, floors, crawl space, cathedral ceilings $1.16 per square foot; flat attic $0.77 per square foot; air sealing $310 / $460 / $620 / $770 per home by tiers of air-leak reduction (over 15%, 25%, 33%, 50%)
facts.eligibility: Efficiency Works assessment first; listed service provider; pre and post blower-door tests and combustion safety test; home at least one year old; over $2,500 needs preapproval
facts.dates: Effective Jan 1, 2026
facts.notes: The sheet's own example (2,000 sq ft attic at $1.16 plus Xcel $1,250 for $3,570) adds an Xcel figure that does not apply to Fort Collins Utilities homes, and uses $1.16 where the flat-attic rate is $0.77, so we do not repeat it.

facts.program: Efficiency Works windows and doors (Fort Collins Utilities)
facts.claim: Windows and sliding glass doors: ENERGY STAR version 6 $3.75 per square foot, version 7 $5.00 per square foot; exterior doors $3.75 per square foot
facts.eligibility: Listed service provider; home at least one year old; ENERGY STAR Northern climate zone; combustion safety test required
facts.dates: Effective Jan 1, 2026
facts.notes: The sheet's example is 20 windows of 20 square feet: $1,500 at Tier 1 and $2,000 at Tier 2.

facts.program: Efficiency Works retail rebates: thermostats, induction, dryers (Fort Collins Utilities)
facts.claim: Smart thermostat up to $50 (central AC or heat pump) or up to $75 for electric baseboard thermostats (minimum two); induction range or cooktop up to $350 replacing gas, up to $50 replacing electric; heat pump dryer up to $50 compact or $100 standard; clothes washer up to $50
facts.eligibility: Fort Collins Utilities customer; apply within 45 days of purchase; new equipment only; photo of the old gas range required for the $350
facts.dates: Revised January 2026
facts.notes: The retrofit HVAC sheet lists smart thermostats at $35 per unit, $70 maximum per home; the retail sheet says up to $50. We quote the retail sheet as up to $50 and tell readers to confirm.

facts.program: Efficiency Works electric panel upgrade and load sharing device (Fort Collins Utilities)
facts.claim: 200-amp or larger panel upgrade $500; load sharing device $250; only with an induction range, Level 2 EV charger, heat pump, heat pump water heater, solar or battery project
facts.eligibility: Licensed electrician; documentation of the paired upgrade
facts.dates: Effective Jan 1, 2026

facts.program: Boulder County EnergySmart income-qualified rebates
facts.claim: 50% of project cost up to $2,000 per year for households at or below 100% of area median income: insulation, air sealing, heat pumps, heat pump water heaters, induction cooktops; also electric panel upgrades and cellular shades. Standard (non income-qualified) rebates were retired in late 2025.
facts.eligibility: Boulder County residents at or below 100% of AMI; site-built and manufactured homes
facts.dates: Work completed and invoiced Jan 1 to Dec 31, 2026; first come, first served
facts.notes: Boulder County also lists Xcel Energy, Longmont, Lyons, Erie, PVREA, United Power and the Colorado RENU loan as other sources.

facts.program: City and County of Denver homeowner heat pump rebate
facts.claim: Denver's current homeowner page lists a Switch Together group buy (savings up to 10% off average install cost) and links to Xcel, the Colorado Energy Office and Power Ahead Colorado; no Denver-funded homeowner heat pump rebate amount is listed there
facts.dates: Group-buy page read 2026-10-05
facts.notes: Search results mention a Denver Climate Action Rebates program that opened Jan 9 and a 2025 notice that the residential heat pump rebate was fully subscribed; we could not open a current Denver page with amounts, so we state no Denver amount.

facts.program: City of Aurora homeowner energy rebates
facts.claim: No City of Aurora homeowner heat pump or insulation rebate could be confirmed from an auroragov.org page
facts.dates: Searched 2026-10-05
facts.notes: Third-party sites list an Aurora heat pump rebate of $250 to $500; we could not read an Aurora page that confirms it, so we do not state it.
